 SBI Defence FOF NFO opens today: HAL to BEL, 5 stocks make up over 50% of underlying ETF portfolio
 By Rajeev Kumar 4 min read | Updated on November 16, 2026, 07:15 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 The fund of funds of SBI Defence ETF FOF opens today, November 16, and closes on November 30. The scheme will hold at least 95% in the SBI BSE India Defence ETF, and has a base expense ratio at 0.90%
 Stock list
 HAL -- BEL -- The NFO of SBI Defence ETF FOF opens on Monday, November 16, 2026. | Image: Shutterstock
 SBI Mutual Fund has launched the SBI BSE India Defence ETF FOF, an open-ended fund of funds that will put its money into a single exchange traded fund tracking the defence theme. The new fund offer opens today, November 16, and closes on November 30, 2026, with units offered at ₹10 each. Here are five things to know about the NFO from scheme information document, and the fund house's announcement.
 Open FREE Demat Account within minutes! Join now 
 First, what exactly is being offered. 
 The scheme will hold between 95% and 100% of its assets in units of the SBI BSE India Defence ETF, with the remaining 0 to 5% in government securities maturing within a year, Treasury bills, triparty repo or units of liquid mutual funds. The FOF's benchmark is the BSE India Defence TRI.

 Second, what sits underneath. 
 The underlying ETF tracks the BSE India Defence index, which, in the document's words, “aims to track the performance of those stocks representing the Defence theme”.
 Companies are drawn from the BSE 1000 universe, with core defence businesses from specified basic industries entering directly, while others are screened through a process that includes membership of the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers.
 The index is top-heavy. As on July 31, 2026, Hindustan Aeronautics carried a 15.70% weight, Bharat Electronics 13.62% and Solar Industries 12.92%, with the ten largest constituents accounting for about 74% of the index.
 Third, what it costs. 
 An exit load of 1% applies to redemptions on or before 15 days from allotment, and nothing after that. The base expense ratio of the fund of funds, including the weighted average of the base expense ratio levied by the underlying scheme, is capped at 0.90% of daily net assets. However, this cap does not cover everything. The document states plainly that investors “will be bearing the recurring expenses of the Scheme in addition to the total expense ratio” of the underlying schemes.
 The scheme has regular and direct plans, and the direct plan carries a lower expense ratio with no commission paid from it.
 Fourth, how you enter and exit. 
 The minimum application during the NFO is ₹5,000, in multiples of Re 1, and the minimum additional purchase is ₹1,000. The minimum redemption is ₹500, or one unit, whichever is lower. Each plan offers growth and income distribution options, with growth as the default.
 The scheme will reopen for continuous subscription within five business days of allotment.
 Fifth, who runs it and what to weigh. 
 Viral Chhadva, who has been with SBI Funds Management since December 2020 and manages several of its passive offerings, is the fund manager.
 Two things are worth weighing before applying: This is a single-theme, single-ETF portfolio.
 There is no second fund manager, no second sector and no stock-level discretion. So the outcome will be the index's outcome, less costs. And the index itself is concentrated, with three stocks accounting for more than 40% of its weight.
 The document also carries the standard caveat that the scheme gives no guarantee of achieving its investment objective.
